label: Luke 18:1
text: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray, and not give up,

label: Luke 18:2
text:
saying,
“There was a judge in a certain city who didn’t fear God, and didn’t respect man.

label: Luke 18:3
text: A widow was in that city, and she often came to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’

label: Luke 18:4
text: He wouldn’t for a while, but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God, nor respect man,

label: Luke 18:5
text: yet because this widow bothers me, I will defend her, or else she will wear me out by her continual coming.’”

label: Luke 18:6
text:
The Lord said,
“Listen to what the unrighteous judge says.

label: Luke 18:7
text: Won’t God avenge his chosen ones, who are crying out to him day and night, and yet he exercises patience with them?

label: Luke 18:8
text: I tell you that he will avenge them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”

label: Luke 18:9
text: He spoke also this parable to certain people who were convinced of their own righteousness, and who despised all others.

label: Luke 18:10
text: “Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.

label: Luke 18:11
text: The Pharisee stood and prayed to himself like this: ‘God, I thank you, that I am not like the rest of men, extortionists, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.

label: Luke 18:12
text: I fast twice a week. I give tithes of all that I get.’

label: Luke 18:13
text: But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’

label: Luke 18:14
text: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”

label: Luke 18:15
text: They were also bringing their babies to him, that he might touch them. But when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.

label: Luke 18:16
text:
Jesus summoned them, saying,
“Allow the little children to come to me, and don’t hinder them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.

label: Luke 18:17
text: Most certainly, I tell you, whoever doesn’t receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”

label: Luke 18:18
text: A certain ruler asked him, saying, “Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”

label: Luke 18:19
text:
Jesus asked him,
“Why do you call me good? No one is good, except one—God.

label: Luke 18:20
text: You know the commandments: ‘Don’t commit adultery,’ ‘Don’t murder,’ ‘Don’t steal,’ ‘Don’t give false testimony,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother.’”

label: Luke 18:21
text: He said, “I have observed all these things from my youth up.”

label: Luke 18:22
text:
When Jesus heard these things, he said to him,
“You still lack one thing. Sell all that you have, and distribute it to the poor. You will have treasure in heaven. Come, follow me.”

label: Luke 18:23
text: But when he heard these things, he became very sad, for he was very rich.

label: Luke 18:24
text:
Jesus, seeing that he became very sad, said,
“How hard it is for those who have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!

label: Luke 18:25
text: For it is easier for a camel to enter in through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”

label: Luke 18:26
text: Those who heard it said, “Then who can be saved?”

label: Luke 18:27
text:
But he said,
“The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.”

label: Luke 18:28
text: Peter said, “Look, we have left everything, and followed you.”

label: Luke 18:29
text:
He said to them,
“Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or wife, or brothers, or parents, or children, for God’s Kingdom’s sake,

label: Luke 18:30
text: who will not receive many times more in this time, and in the world to come, eternal life.”

label: Luke 18:31
text:
He took the twelve aside, and said to them,
“Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things that are written through the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be completed.

label: Luke 18:32
text: For he will be delivered up to the Gentiles, will be mocked, treated shamefully, and spit on.

label: Luke 18:33
text: They will scourge and kill him. On the third day, he will rise again.”

label: Luke 18:34
text: They understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them, and they didn’t understand the things that were said.

label: Luke 18:35
text: As he came near Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the road, begging.

label: Luke 18:36
text: Hearing a multitude going by, he asked what this meant.

label: Luke 18:37
text: They told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.

label: Luke 18:38
text: He cried out, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”

label: Luke 18:39
text: Those who led the way rebuked him, that he should be quiet; but he cried out all the more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”

label: Luke 18:40
text: Standing still, Jesus commanded him to be brought to him. When he had come near, he asked him,

label: Luke 18:41
text:
“What do you want me to do?”
He said, “Lord, that I may see again.”

label: Luke 18:42
text:
Jesus said to him,
“Receive your sight. Your faith has healed you.”

label: Luke 18:43
text: Immediately he received his sight, and followed him, glorifying God. All the people, when they saw it, praised God.

label: A widow pleaded repeatedly before a city judge
statement: In the parable's setting, a widow could bring a case against an adversary before a judge in a city, and could keep coming to him until he granted justice. The judge is a parable character; evidence attests the institution of city courts, not that the parable was told.

label: The Pharisee fasts twice a week
statement: The Pharisee in the parable says 'I fast twice a week'. Evidence attests the custom of twice-weekly voluntary fasting in that period, not that the parable was told.

label: The Pharisee tithes all that he gets
statement: The Pharisee in the parable says 'I give tithes of all that I get' - tithing beyond the strictly required (crops grown in the land) to all income. Evidence attests the tithing custom, not that the parable was told.

label: A certain ruler, very rich, asked about eternal life and went away sad
statement: A certain ruler (archon) asked Jesus what he should do to inherit eternal life, claimed to have kept the commandments from his youth, and went away sad, for he was very rich.

label: The third passion prediction: delivered to the Gentiles, mocked, spat on, scourged, killed, rising the third day
statement: Jesus said (18:31-33) that the Son of Man would be delivered up to the Gentiles, mocked, treated shamefully and spit on, scourged and killed, and rise the third day. The saying is recorded neutrally; evidence can bear only on the events said to come, not on the saying.

label: A blind beggar at Jericho cries 'Son of David' and receives his sight
statement: As Jesus drew near Jericho, a certain blind beggar sat by the road, cried out 'Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me', and at Jesus's word received his sight and followed, glorifying God. The healing itself is a miracle claim; external evidence can bear only on the setting.

label: Josephus, Ant. 4.8.14 (seven judges in every city)
author: Josephus

label: Mishnah Taanit 2:2 (communal fasts set on Monday and Thursday)
author: Rabbinic tradition

label: Didache 8:1 (fasting on 'the Preparation')
author: Unknown early Christian author
date: c. 50-120 CE (scholars place it in the first or early second century)

label: Wikisource: Josephus, Antiquities 4.8.14 (judges in every city)
title: The Antiquities of the Jews, Book IV (Whiston)
excerpt: Let there be seven men to judge in every city, (20) and these such as have been before most zealous in the exercise of virtue and righteousness. Let every judge have two officers allotted him out of the tribe of Levi.

label: Sefaria: Mishnah Taanit 2:2 (fasts on Monday, Thursday, Monday)
title: Mishnah Taanit 2 (William Davidson translation)
excerpt: Rather, the first set of three fasts is on a Monday, Thursday, and the following Monday, and the second set of three is on a Thursday, Monday, and the following Thursday.

label: Many times more in this time, eternal life in the age to come
statement: Everyone who leaves house or family for the Kingdom of God will receive many times more in this time, and eternal life in the age to come (Luke's 'many times more'; Matthew 19:29 says 'a hundred times').
